content:
With @Zhidong Huang , we have written a formalization of the self-contained and elegant proof of the transcendence of π given by Niven in 1939.

I was wondering whether this would be of interest to the mathlib community, and whether it could be an acceptable series of PRs.

This is not the usual proof found in textbooks, since the result is often derived directly as a corollary of the Lindemann–Weierstrass theorem (which I think is also currently being integrated into mathlib). How does mathlib usually deal with having different proofs of the same result?

In general Mathlib contains only one proof, of the most general result, so we will probably go the Lindemann-Weierstrass route. However, if along the way you have identified results of general interest that were useful to you and are missing from Mathlib, they would definitely be welcome additions.

I see! I'd be curious to see whether this changes someday. This is more philosophical, but mathematics is full of interesting ways to reach the same result, and maybe one day the mathlib community will want to make room for that.

By the way, I noticed that some theorems on the 100 Theorems list are credited as "outside of mathlib." Since our formalization probably won’t make it into mathlib, do you think we could make a PR to have it listed that way too?

Yes, adding your formalization to the 100 theorems list is absolutely a good idea.

I don't think Mathlib will change in the philosophy to have one proof of each result. Mathlib is not supposed to be the unique library of mathematics in Lean, but a curated reference that people can use. So the goal should not be to get something into Mathlib (unless you want to make sure that it can be used by others), the goal is to do beautiful mathematics, and if Mathlib can help then that's great. I think your formalization fits perfectly well this description!
Yes, such a PR is definitely welcome
@Sébastien Gouëzel great comment thank you!
@Samuël Borza also note that during your formalization work you will most likely find small results that are missing in mathlib, and those are a very welcome contribution!

Samuël Borza said in #mathlib4 > Direct proof of the transcendence of π:

mathematics is full of interesting ways to reach the same result, and maybe one day the mathlib community will want to make room for that.

I would personally be happy for "second proofs" to be hosted in the Archive folder of mathlib

@Riccardo Brasca Indeed, I will try my best to contribute the small results we had to prove into mathlib. If done well, the final argument would fit into one smaller file that could potentially be in the archive folder (thanks @Yaël Dillies for the idea!)
